FRENCH — TERMLY EXAM #8
====

GRADE: Grade 12
SUBJECT: FRENCH
TIME ALLOWED: 1 hour 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Critical Listening, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Critical Listening.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Critical Listening.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Critical Listening.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Critical Listening.

2. The French word for “book” is: (1 mark)
   A. livre
   B. chaise
   C. fenêtre
   D. porte

3. “Bonjour” is used to say: (1 mark)
   A. Thank you
   B. Excuse me
   C. Good night only
   D. Good morning / hello

4. When practising Listening for Information, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for Information.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Listening for Information.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Listening for Information.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Listening for Information.

5. When practising Interactive speaking, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Interactive speaking.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Interactive speaking.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Interactive speaking.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Interactive speaking.

6. When practising Grammar ● Language structures ● Language structures ● Language structures ● Lang, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar ● Language structures ● Language structures ● Language structures ● Lang.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Grammar ● Language structures ● Language structures ● Language structures ● Lang.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar ● Language structures ● Language structures ● Language structures ● Lang.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Grammar ● Language structures ● Language structures ● Language structures ● Lang.

7. When practising Persuasive Speaking, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Persuasive Speaking.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Persuasive Speaking.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Persuasive Speaking.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Persuasive Speaking.

8. When practising Intensive Listening, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Intensive Listening.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Intensive Listening.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Intensive Listening.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Intensive Listening.

9. When practising Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Reading.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Reading.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Reading.

10. When practising Reading for information, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading for information.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Reading for information.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Reading for information.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Reading for information.

11. When practising Writing ● Descriptive writing ● Expository writing ● Descriptive writing ● Proce, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Writing ● Descriptive writing ● Expository writing ● Descriptive writing ● Proce.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Writing ● Descriptive writing ● Expository writing ● Descriptive writing ● Proce.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Writing ● Descriptive writing ● Expository writing ● Descriptive writing ● Proce.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing ● Descriptive writing ● Expository writing ● Descriptive writing ● Proce.

12. When practising Informative Speaking, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Informative Speaking.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Informative Speaking.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Informative Speaking.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Informative Speaking.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Reading and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Listening for Information and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Writing ● Descriptive writing ● Expository writing ● Descriptive writing ● Proce and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Interactive speaking and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

17. In three clear sentences, explain Grammar ● Language structures ● Language structures ● Language structures ● Lang and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Intensive Listening and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

MARKING SCHEME
====

1. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Critical Listening.

2. A — livre

3. D — Good morning / hello

4. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for Information.

5. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Interactive speaking.

6. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar ● Language structures ● Language structures ● Language structures ● Lang.

7. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Persuasive Speaking.

8. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Intensive Listening.

9. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading.

10. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading for information.

11. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing ● Descriptive writing ● Expository writing ● Descriptive writing ● Proce.

12. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Informative Speaking.

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Reading; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Listening for Information; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Interactive speaking; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

17. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Grammar ● Language structures ● Language structures ● Language structures ● Lang; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

18. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Intensive Listening; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
